column11: Voyxact (sibeprenlimab, Otsuka, FDA accelerated approval 25 November 2025) at its published annual list of $390,000: pharmaphorum, 'Otsuka's Voyxact faces rival as FDA okays Vera IgAN drug' (https://pharmaphorum.com/news/otsukas-voyxact-faces-rival-fda-okays-vera-igan-drug). Cross-check: ICER's IgAN evidence report press release (icer.org) gives Voyxact an estimated annual net price of $292,500, which is exactly 75% of $390,000.
column12: Voyxact is the closest marketed comparator: the same target (APRIL), the same disease and the same route. The brief ranks a named published annual list above the CMS convention, so $390,000 replaces the $399,499 read off CMS Medicare Quarterly Part D, Q1 2026 ($4,640,341 over 151 claims, $30,730.73 a claim, x13). That CMS figure sits 2.4% above the $30,000-a-dose list, as Part D gross cost does, because it carries pharmacy dispensing. The price is per patient-year, not per dose, so zigakibart's every-two-weeks schedule does not double it; that Novartis prices to the class is a judgement. Case against: Trutakna (atacicept, Vera), approved 7 July 2026, launched at $425,000 a year (same pharmaphorum article), so the class price is not settled at Voyxact's; Novartis could also price below both as a later entrant. Book follow-up: the povetacicept and sefaxersen seeds still carry $399,499, and the sefaxersen seed calls it the 'published US list', which it is not.

column11: ICER, B-Cell Directed Therapies for IgA Nephropathy, Evidence Report, 9 February 2026, Table E2.3: IPD Analytics forecasts a 25% discount from WAC for sibeprenlimab (as carried on the povetacicept and sefaxersen seeds)
column12: Net is 75% of list. Direction checked: this is the share OFF list. The anchor is now Voyxact's published list (WAC) of $390,000, so per the brief neither house convention (0.5 on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price, 0.056604 on Part B) applies and the discount is sourced: ICER's net of $292,500 on the $390,000 list is 25% off. Keeping the value keeps the three IgAN B-cell assets consistent. Case against: IPD Analytics' 25% is a forecast for a first entrant; a fourth APRIL-blocking entrant may need deeper rebates to win formulary position.

column12: JUDGEMENT on timing. The sefaxersen seed measured Fabhalta going from its positive IgAN interim to accelerated approval in 10.2 months. On that pace, a mid-2027 readout gives approval around Q2 2028, so 2029 is the first full year. Case for 2028: a readout early in H1 2027 plus a priority review would put most of 2028 on the market. The extension NCT06858319 has a primary completion of 2031-06-25, but it is not the registration trial. BEYOND's own primary completion is 2027-08-10 (estimated; ClinicalTrials.gov v2 as held in the book's trials table, 383 enrolled, active not recruiting), which fits a week-40 proteinuria readout in H1 2027 for an accelerated filing and the 104-week data after it.

column12: Carried so the three IgAN B-cell assets share one label pool. BEYOND enrols adults with biopsy-proven IgAN, total urine protein of 1.0 g a day or more and UPCR of 0.7 g/g or more, eGFR of 30 or more, on maximally tolerated RAS blockade (WCN24-1837 abstract; IgAN Foundation study page), so the 1 g a day filter matches the trial. The CKD 1 to 4 filter keeps stage 4 (eGFR 15 to 29), which BEYOND does not enrol; Voyxact's label ('adults with primary IgAN at risk for disease progression') carries no eGFR floor, which is why the book keeps it. Case against: were the label to follow BEYOND's eGFR 30 floor, Caster's 42% at CKD 4 or 5 leaves 58% in stages 1 to 3, and 0.58 x 0.850 = 0.493.
